q: In which year did Pakistan come into being?
x: Pakistan became independent on 14 August 1947.

q: Who was the first Governor-General of Pakistan?
x: Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah was the first Governor-General.

q: Who was the first Prime Minister of Pakistan?
x: Liaquat Ali Khan became the first Prime Minister in 1947.

q: The Lahore Resolution was passed in which year?
x: It was passed on 23 March 1940 at Minto Park (now Iqbal Park), Lahore.

q: What is the national language of Pakistan?
x: Urdu is the national language; English is also an official language.

q: What is the capital of Pakistan?
x: Islamabad became the capital in the 1960s, replacing Karachi.

q: Which is the highest mountain in Pakistan?
x: K2 (8,611 m) is the highest in Pakistan and second highest in the world.

q: Which is the longest river in Pakistan?
x: The Indus is Pakistan's longest river.

q: Who wrote the national anthem of Pakistan?
x: Hafeez Jalandhari wrote the words; Ahmed G. Chagla composed the music.

q: Who is known as the national poet of Pakistan?
x: Allama Muhammad Iqbal is the national poet.

q: Which is the largest province of Pakistan by area?
x: Balochistan is the largest by area; Punjab has the most people.

q: What is the national flower of Pakistan?
x: Jasmine is the national flower.

q: What is the national animal of Pakistan?
x: The Markhor, a wild goat, is the national animal.

q: What is the national bird of Pakistan?
x: The Chukar partridge is the national bird.

q: In which year was Pakistan's first constitution adopted?
x: The first constitution came into force on 23 March 1956.

q: The current constitution of Pakistan was adopted in which year?
x: The 1973 Constitution is in force today.

q: Which city is known as the City of Lights?
x: Karachi is often called the City of Lights.

q: Which city is called the City of Saints?
x: Multan is called the City of Saints because of its many shrines.

q: Where is the Badshahi Mosque?
x: The Badshahi Mosque in Lahore was built by Mughal emperor Aurangzeb.

q: Which pass connects Pakistan and Afghanistan near Peshawar?
x: The Khyber Pass links Peshawar with Afghanistan.

q: The Khunjerab Pass connects Pakistan with which country?
x: The Karakoram Highway crosses into China at the Khunjerab Pass.

q: Who founded the All-India Muslim League?
o: Group of Muslim leaders at Dhaka in 1906
x: It was founded at Dhaka in 1906 by a group of Muslim leaders.

q: Who founded Aligarh's Muhammadan Anglo-Oriental College?
x: Sir Syed Ahmad Khan founded it in 1875; it became Aligarh Muslim University.

q: Which is the largest city of Pakistan by population?
x: Karachi is the largest city.

q: What is the currency of Pakistan?
x: The Pakistani Rupee (PKR) is issued by the State Bank of Pakistan.

q: Tarbela Dam is built on which river?
x: Tarbela Dam is on the Indus River.

q: Mangla Dam is built on which river?
x: Mangla Dam is on the Jhelum River.

q: How many continents are there?
x: Asia, Africa, North America, South America, Antarctica, Europe and Australia.

q: Which is the largest ocean?
x: The Pacific is the largest and deepest ocean.

q: Which is the largest country by area?
x: Russia is the largest country by area.

q: Which planet is known as the Red Planet?
x: Mars looks red because of iron oxide on its surface.

q: Which is the largest planet in our solar system?
x: Jupiter is the largest planet.

q: What is the capital of Turkey?
x: Ankara is the capital; Istanbul is the largest city.

q: What is the capital of Saudi Arabia?
x: Riyadh is the capital of Saudi Arabia.

q: Which is the longest river in the world (by most common measure)?
x: The Nile is usually counted as the longest river.

q: Which is the highest mountain in the world?
x: Mount Everest is 8,849 m high.

q: The United Nations was founded in which year?
x: The UN was founded in 1945, after the Second World War.

q: Where is the headquarters of the United Nations?
x: The UN headquarters is in New York.

q: Which is the largest desert in the world (hot desert)?
x: The Sahara is the largest hot desert.

q: How many players are there in a cricket team on the field?
x: Each side has 11 players on the field.

q: How many players are there in a football team on the field?
x: Each side has 11 players, including the goalkeeper.

q: Which country hosted the 1992 Cricket World Cup that Pakistan won?
x: Pakistan won the 1992 World Cup held in Australia and New Zealand.

q: What is the currency of Japan?
x: The Japanese currency is the Yen.

q: Which country is called the Land of the Rising Sun?
x: Japan is called the Land of the Rising Sun.

q: How many days are there in a leap year?
x: A leap year has 366 days, with 29 days in February.

q: What is the capital of Malaysia?
x: Kuala Lumpur is the capital of Malaysia.

q: How many surahs are there in the Holy Quran?
x: The Quran has 114 surahs.

q: Which is the first surah of the Holy Quran?
x: Surah Al-Fatiha is the opening surah.

q: Which is the longest surah of the Holy Quran?
x: Surah Al-Baqarah is the longest surah.

q: How many pillars of Islam are there?
x: Shahadah, Salah, Zakat, Sawm and Hajj.

q: In which month do Muslims fast?
x: Muslims fast in the month of Ramadan.

q: How many times a day is Salah obligatory?
x: Five daily prayers: Fajr, Zuhr, Asr, Maghrib and Isha.

q: In which city was the Holy Prophet (PBUH) born?
x: The Holy Prophet (PBUH) was born in Makkah.

q: The migration from Makkah to Madinah is called?
x: The Hijrah marks the start of the Islamic calendar.

q: Who was the first Caliph of Islam?
x: Hazrat Abu Bakr Siddique (RA) was the first Caliph.

q: Which surah is called the heart of the Quran?
x: Surah Yaseen is commonly called the heart of the Quran.

q: How many months are there in the Islamic calendar?
x: The Hijri calendar has 12 lunar months.

q: What is the first month of the Islamic calendar?
x: Muharram is the first month of the Hijri year.

q: Zakat is usually paid at what rate on savings above nisab?
x: Zakat is 2.5% of eligible wealth held for a lunar year above the nisab.

q: Hajj is performed in which Islamic month?
x: Hajj takes place in Dhul Hijjah.

q: Which angel brought revelation to the Holy Prophet (PBUH)?
x: Hazrat Jibrail (AS) brought the revelation.

q: In which cave did the first revelation come?
x: The first revelation came in the Cave of Hira.

q: The first battle in Islam was?
x: The Battle of Badr took place in 2 AH.

q: Choose the synonym of "Abundant":
x: Abundant means existing in large amounts.

q: Choose the antonym of "Ancient":
x: The opposite of ancient is modern.

q: Choose the correct spelling:
x: Remember: i before e, except after c.

q: Choose the correct sentence:
x: With he/she/it, use doesn't plus the base verb.

q: Fill in the blank: He has been living here ___ 2015.
x: Use "since" with a point in time; "for" with a length of time.

q: Choose the synonym of "Diligent":
x: Diligent means showing care and effort.

q: Choose the antonym of "Generous":
x: The opposite of generous is selfish or mean.

q: What is the plural of "child"?
x: Child has an irregular plural: children.

q: Choose the correct word: I am interested ___ learning English.
x: We say "interested in".

q: What does the idiom "a piece of cake" mean?
x: "A piece of cake" means very easy.

q: What does "once in a blue moon" mean?
x: It means very rarely.

q: Choose the correct past tense of "go":
x: Go, went, gone.

q: Choose the synonym of "Brief":
x: Brief means short in time or length.

q: Choose the correctly punctuated sentence:
x: "It's" is short for "it is".

q: What is the chemical formula of water?
x: Water is two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom.

q: Which gas do plants absorb from the air?
x: Plants take in carbon dioxide for photosynthesis.

q: What is the boiling point of water at sea level?
x: Water boils at 100 °C at normal air pressure.

q: Which organ pumps blood around the body?
x: The heart pumps blood.

q: Which vitamin do we get from sunlight?
x: The skin makes vitamin D in sunlight.

q: How many bones are there in an adult human body?
x: An adult has 206 bones.

q: What is the centre of an atom called?
x: The nucleus holds protons and neutrons.

q: Which is the closest star to the Earth?
x: The Sun is the nearest star.

q: What is the SI unit of force?
x: Force is measured in newtons.

q: Which blood group is called the universal donor?
x: O negative red cells can usually be given to anyone.

q: What gas do humans breathe out the most of, compared with what they breathe in?
x: We breathe out more carbon dioxide than we breathe in.

q: Which part of the plant makes food?
x: Leaves make food by photosynthesis.

q: What does CPU stand for?
x: The CPU is the main processor of a computer.

q: Which of these is an input device?
x: A keyboard sends input to the computer.

q: What does RAM stand for?
x: RAM is the computer's working memory.

q: 1 kilobyte is equal to how many bytes (as usually taught)?
x: In computing, 1 KB is usually taught as 1024 bytes.

q: Which shortcut copies selected text in Windows?
x: Ctrl + C copies; Ctrl + V pastes.

q: Which shortcut undoes the last action?
x: Ctrl + Z undoes.

q: Which of these is a spreadsheet program?
x: Excel is a spreadsheet program.

q: What does "www" stand for?
x: www stands for World Wide Web.

q: Which of these is an operating system?
x: Windows is an operating system.

q: What does PDF stand for?
x: PDF stands for Portable Document Format.

q: Which Excel function adds numbers?
x: =SUM() adds a range of numbers.

q: Which device connects a home network to the internet?
x: A router connects your network to the internet.

q: What does "URL" stand for?
x: A URL is a web address.
